textContent.text: As an avid stamp collector, my heart skipped a beat when I saw an old-fashioned storefront with a sign that read "The Post Office" over the front door. It seemed like just the type of place that offers collectors like me a chance to find some really rare stamps. My car pretty much drove itself into the parking lot! "Take my money!" I practically shouted. I couldn't wait to get a look at the stamps and possibly add to my collection.

Bells jingled as I opened the fancy door. My excitement only increased as I spotted an antique wooden desk and a wall of old combination lockboxes. But my euphoria turned quickly to frustration as I looked around. I felt like I had been duped! Although the interior was decorated to look like a post office from the 1800s, the waitstaff carrying trays of food was a clue that I had been deceived about the purpose of the place.

textContent.text: After scanning the description on its website, I made a spontaneous decision to stay at the Apple Bear Lodge in the Great Smoky Mountains last weekend. There were many phenomenal aspects to this rustic-style lodge. The beds were luxuriously soft, there was a spacious deck to enjoy the outdoors, and the water pressure in the shower was fantastic!

My only real disappointment was that the lodge was located in a suburban subdivision instead of the picturesque mountain setting I had envisioned. The photographs online must have been taken on the roof, because when I looked out my window, all I could see was the house next door. Those glorious mountain vistas were completely obscured by the neighboring homes. Next time, I will read the reviews more carefully before booking a trip.

textContent.text: Since the age of nine, I have made riding waterslides my sole hobby, so some would call me a waterslide aficionado. I have always dreamed of working at a water park. Imagine being able to test out the rides with no lines! So, when I was offered a position at Slides Galore this past June, I jumped at the opportunity. But nothing could have prepared me for the things they don't tell you about working in a water park.

First, there's the never-ending task of cleaning the filters. Over the course of the summer, I fished out a million pairs of sunglasses, countless flip-flops, and even a nose ring (don't ask). Then there's keeping the tubes inflated, the trash cans emptied, and the sunscreen shelves stocked. As if all that isn't enough, every free second is spent listening to guests complain when the aforementioned tasks are left undone. So, despite being surrounded by exciting water rides, people who work in water parks rarely have time to enjoy them.

textContent.text: When you show up for your three-hour "cave crawl" at Cold River Caverns, be sure you're dressed appropriately. The website suggests sturdy boots, pants, and warm, form-fitting clothing. I recommend work gloves and knee pads, too. They're not kidding when they call it a crawl! Definitely don't wear anything you want to keep clean; you'll likely be caked with mud when you emerge into the light.

With the right clothing and mindset, though, cave lovers like me are in for a marvelous caving adventure. After descending steeply into darkness, you'll cross a swinging suspension bridge over the cold, dark river. With your headlamp, which is provided for you, you'll view colorful rock formations and spot cave critters like see-through shrimp and eyeless crawfish. These caves are unlike any I've explored before. For an incredible underground adventure, do yourself a favor: dress properly, love the mud, and take the leap—or rather, the crawl—into Cold River Caverns.

textContent.text: Of all my hobbies, puttering around in my vegetable garden is my favorite. My friends joke that I treat my plants like they are my children. So, when I won a once-in-a-lifetime trip to Switzerland, I was hesitant to leave my beloved baby veggies at home alone. Who would sing lullabies to the carrots? Who would know that the tomatoes needed exactly seven minutes of watering, not a second more or less?

I needn't have worried; the folks from Petunia's Garden Keepers treated my plants like they were their own. When I returned, my green beans were flourishing and there wasn't a single squash bug to be found on my zucchini. I daresay my plants actually missed the attentive and affectionate crew from Petunia's when I returned. Now I finally feel comfortable traveling and am already looking into a trip to Mexico next spring.

textContent.text: Sweet, buttery, crumbly; in a word, perfect—Recipe Room's shortbread is the cookie recipe of my dreams. But baker beware: these are addictive! In fact, my friends polished off a platter of them in a matter of minutes, so be forewarned and make at least a double batch.

Not only does the recipe stand on its own, but it's also an excellent starting point for variations. I used vanilla extract the first time, with fabulous results. The next time, I added orange juice for a mouthwateringly refreshing flavor. The next time around, I plan on adding lemon zest for extra zing. I'll bet I could substitute peppermint and that would be delicious, too.

Here's my favorite trick: I replace one-quarter cup of the flour with cornstarch to produce a softer—and absolutely scrumptious—cookie. If you're in the mood for shortbread, you should definitely try this recipe. The possibilities are endless!

textContent.text: When you show up for your three-hour "cave crawl" at Cold River Caverns, be sure you're dressed appropriately. The website suggests sturdy boots, pants, and warm, form-fitting clothing. I recommend work gloves and knee pads, too. They're not kidding when they call it a crawl! After descending steeply into darkness, you'll cross a swinging suspension bridge over the cold, dark river. With your headlamp, which is provided for you, you'll view colorful rock formations and spot cave critters like see-through shrimp and eyeless crawfish. These caves are unlike any I've explored before. For an incredible underground adventure, do yourself a favor: dress properly, love the mud, and take the leap—or rather, the crawl—into Cold River Caverns.

textContent.text: When you show up for your three-hour "cave crawl" at Cold River Caverns, be sure you're dressed appropriately. The website suggests sturdy boots, pants, and warm, form-fitting clothing. I recommend work gloves and knee pads, too. They're not kidding when they call it a crawl! With the right clothing and mindset, though, cave lovers like me are in for a marvelous caving adventure. After descending steeply into darkness, you'll cross a swinging suspension bridge over the cold, dark river. With your headlamp, which is provided for you, you'll view colorful rock formations and spot cave critters like see-through shrimp and eyeless crawfish. These caves are unlike any I've explored before. For an incredible underground adventure, do yourself a favor: dress properly, love the mud, and take the leap—or rather, the crawl—into Cold River Caverns.

textContent.text: Of all my hobbies, puttering around in my vegetable garden is my favorite. My friends joke that I treat my plants like they are my children. I daresay my plants actually missed the attentive and affectionate crew from Petunia's when I returned. Now I finally feel comfortable traveling and am already looking into a trip to Mexico next spring.

textContent.text: As an avid stamp collector, my heart skipped a beat when I saw an old-fashioned storefront with a sign that read "The Post Office" over the front door.
